texts: Most lung abscesses heal with antibiotics and drainage, so the size of the cavity alone is not an indication for resection: A is the answer.
Resection is indicated when a cavitating cancer cannot be excluded, for an infected sequestration, for a bronchopleural fistula and for recurrent or massive haemoptysis.
Failure of medical treatment is another indication; large cavities are more likely to fail, but are first treated medically.
